papers.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
papers.abstract: Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly. We propose two approaches guided by the implicit local and global constraints a target PD imposes. The local approach builds degree-based PD-equivalent graphs iteratively, and we prove that every output realizes the target PD and that every degree-based PD-equivalent graph is reachable. However, as shown thereafter, local generation necessarily trades off between sample diversity and reaching infeasible states. We therefore recast generation as a global constraint satisfaction problem with a complete encoding solvable by modern constraint programming solvers. This is applicable to any vertex-based permutation equivariant filtration scheme and is minimal under the degree filtration. Experiments on four standard graph generation benchmarks confirm that both methods realize the target PD exactly. Together, our methods provide a principled treatment of strict topology-compliant graph generation. Code is available at https://github.com/Aalto-QuML/ExactCompliance.

papers.title: Characterization of $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of small rank
papers.abstract: The $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a polynomial map is a quadratic enrichment of the classical Milnor number, defined as the local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree of the gradient. We study which elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms arise as $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers. Over fields of characteristic not $2$, $3$, or $5$, we show that every element of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $7$ that is a local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree is also an $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number. Unlike for local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees, however, in general not all $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers can be obtained from two-variable polynomials. Over an arbitrary field of characteristic not $2$, $3$, $5$, or $7$, we characterize the elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $8$ that are $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of two-variable polynomials. Over subfields of $\mathbb{R}$, this implies that there are local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees of ranks $4$, $6$, and $8$ that are not the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a two-variable polynomial. We also prove that under a mild hypothesis one can reduce the number of variables of a polynomial while preserving the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number up to multiplication by a unit.

papers.title: Oka realizations, fundamental groups, and holomorphic cofibrations
papers.abstract: The homotopy types of Oka manifolds are exactly those of countable finite-dimensional CW complexes. We construct realizations as open subsets of complex Euclidean spaces with explicit dimension bounds. Other realizations have good open covers by sets biholomorphic to $\C^N$, with prescribed finite nerves, or are unions of Fatou--Bieberbach domains whose nonempty finite intersections are again Fatou--Bieberbach domains. Every nonempty Stein manifold admits a proper holomorphic embedding into an Oka open subset of some $\C^N$, and this embedding is a homotopy equivalence. We obtain holomorphic representatives of ordinary and generalized cohomology classes, and realize every countable group as the fundamental group of an Oka domain in $\C^5$. The fundamental groups of algebraically elliptic manifolds are precisely the finite groups, and every virtually abelian K\"ahler group is the fundamental group of a projective Oka manifold. Finally, we classify holomorphic cofibrations in L\'arusson's intermediate model structures and establish factorizations over aspherical targets into proper holomorphic embeddings and holomorphic fibre bundles with Oka fibre.

papers.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra
papers.abstract: We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology. We exhibit the Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectrum $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{F}_2$ as a $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectrum, the $p$-local Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ (except for $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/4$) and $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ as $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}_{(p)}$-Thom spectra, and the connective complex K-theory spectrum $ku$ as $\mathbb{E}_1$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectra. We accompany these ``go" results with ``no-go" results that show these ``go" results do not admit $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-refinements.

papers.title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology. This result enables the explicit computation of the hyperoctahedral homology of the universal enveloping algebras of involutive (DG) Lie algebras. For group algebras $k[\Gamma]$ equipped with the involution $g \mapsto g^{-1}$, we relate the involutive representation homology of $k[\Gamma]$ to the representation homology of the group $\Gamma$ with coefficients in $\mu_2$, and we show that the latter is the homology of the loop space of the mod $2$ Dold-Thom space of $B\Gamma$; more generally, we compute the representation homology of $\Gamma$ with coefficients in an arbitrary diagonalizable group scheme. As a consequence, the hyperoctahedral homology of $k[\Gamma]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ in characteristic $0$, for every $\Gamma$.

papers.title: Monophobic Neighborhoods of Cubes
papers.abstract: We define a $d$-cube in a graph $G$ to be monophobic in $G$ if, whenever it supports a $d$-face of a discrete singular $d+1$-cube, it must also support another face. In many cases, the presence of such cubes implies the nontriviality of discrete cubical homology and homotopy groups associated with $G$. We describe several large classes of examples and characterize the property completely when $d=2$.

papers.title: Topological realizations of finite posets
papers.abstract: I introduce a new class of cell complexes, called CL-complexes, that provide alternative topological realizations of finite posets. Each realization of a given poset has the same homotopy type as the order complex of that, so in some sense these spaces do not provide anything really new. Their value is that they enable short transparent proofs of standard results in poset homotopy. These include Quillen's Theorem A for finite posets, the Nerve Theorem for good covers of a topological space, and Sheehy's multicover generalization of the Nerve Theorem. Order complexes retain a special status: the order complex of a finite poset admits CL-complex structures both for the poset itself and for its opposite poset. The definition of CL-complexes is motivated by an elementary generalization of the Carrier Lemma of J. W. Walker, which in its original form constructs a canonical homotopy class of maps from a simplicial complex to a space covered by a suitable family of contractible sets. In the generalized lemma, the role played by simplicial complexes and the role played by spaces covered by contractible sets can both be fulfilled by CL-complexes. This sets up an equivalence of categories that tacitly underlies our approach.

papers.title: Geodesic Models for Loop Spaces on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: A topological group, defined in terms of ``composable minimal geodesics'' is constructed and shown to be homotopy equivalent to the pointed loop space of a path-connected, simply connected Riemannian manifold $M$ of positive convexity radius. This construction is analogous to John Milnor's free group model for the pointed loop space of a connected simplicial complex. Related models built from composable minimal geodesics are also obtained for the free loop space of $M$ and for the space of maps from any finite two-dimensional CW-complex into $M$.

papers.title: Koszul Duality in an Equivariant Context
papers.abstract: This article takes steps to show that an equivariant version of the well known phenomena of Koszul Duality can be formulated in a manner not considered prior: via dg (co)algebra valued functors on the orbit category. As such techniques used in this article mix traditional and modern categorical methods in homotopy theory.

papers.title: Equivariant formality for rational $\C_{p^k}$-spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss equivariant formality for spaces equipped with a primary cyclic group action. We study the behavior of equivariant formality with some topological constructions. The algebraic complexity needs to deal with injectivity. In the end, we discuss equivariant intrinsic formality.

papers.title: Persistence diagrams of finite topological spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply persistent homology to study finite topological spaces by associating persistence diagrams with their elements through the furtherness function. This approach enables us to classify elements according to their topological evolution within the space. We further establish a bottleneck stability theorem showing that the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams associated with two elements is bounded above by their mutual furtherness.

papers.title: Models for dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories III: Univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and unitarily complete dagger Segal anima
papers.abstract: We identify the $(\infty,1)$-category presented by the dagger Bergner, dagger Joyal, and dagger Rezk models of Parts I and II with that of univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories. We first construct a realization--nerve adjunction between reversal simplicial anima and Hermitian flags. We prove that its nerve restricts to an equivalence between flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and dagger Segal anima, under which univalence corresponds to unitary completeness. We then construct the adjunctions for univalentization and Hermitian completion and identify univalentization with unitary completion.

papers.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
papers.abstract: The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[ \beta_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.

papers.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.

papers.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
papers.abstract: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.

papers.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic. The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved, proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest. Concurrently, another counterexample (of very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.

papers.title: The Becker--Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example based on units of group rings
papers.abstract: We show by explicit counterexample that the Becker--Gottlieb transfer cannot be made functorial. A different counterexample using rational homotopy theory was discovered concurrently by the third author and Robin Stoll.

papers.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of $\mathbb{R}P^2\times S^2$ and a Braid for non-orientable $4$-Manifolds
papers.abstract: We compute the group of based homotopy classes of self-homotopy equivalences of the non-orientable $4$-manifold $\RP^2\times S^2$. It is an elementary abelian $2$-group of rank $5$. The subgroup of classes whose based lift to the universal cover $S^2\times S^2$ has degree $+1$ has rank $4$ and is isomorphic to the group of free homotopy classes. The group maps onto the group of self-equivalences of the algebraic $2$-type, which has order $8$, with kernel $\pi_4(\RP^2\times S^2)\cong(\Z/2)^2$ generated by pinch-fold maps; that these maps are independent is shown by an adjunction argument. We then construct a non-orientable analogue of the Hambleton--Kreck braid of exact sequences in dimension $4$, for non-orientable manifolds with spin universal cover, stated for finite fundamental group. We apply the braid to $\RP^2\times S^2$ and to $\RP^4$, and for the Hambleton--Hillman manifold with fundamental group $(\Z/2)^2$ we determine the normal $1$-type and show that self-equivalences act on $\pi_2$ through diagonal sign matrices. For $\RP^2\times S^2$ the pinch-fold maps are detected by twisted spin bordism, and, assuming facts from surgery theory stated as hypotheses, exactly one of the three non-trivial pinch-fold maps is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

papers.title: A higher categorical approach to graded bivariant $K$-theories for Real $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We present an $\infty$-categorical refinement of classical $KK$-theory and $E$-theory for graded, $G$-equivariant for a locally compact second countable group $G$, Real $C^*$-algebras. As a consequence, we obtain a couple of fiber sequences connecting the different $K$-theory spectra, and explicitly analyse the induced endomorphisms on $K_0$-groups. We also answer precisely some folklore questions in the area. Among other things, we show that graded $KK$- and $E$-categories are not a Dwyer-Kan localization of graded $C^*$-algebras.

papers.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
papers.abstract: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.

papers.title: Groups with the fixed-point property
papers.abstract: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

papers.title: On finite dimensionality of homology of subalgebras of vector fields
papers.abstract: We show that finite tensor products of modules of tensor fields are Noetherian modules over any graded Lie subalgebra of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$. As a corollary, we prove the conjecture of I.\,M. Gelfand, announced at the ICM in Nice in 1970, on the finite-dimensionality of the continuous cohomology of graded Lie subalgebras of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of formal vector fields $\mathcal{W}_n$. We also prove that tensor products of modules of densities are Noetherian over the Witt Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on the punctured line. Moreover, for a weight $\lambda\neq0,1$ every nonzero submodule of the symmetric power $S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$ contains $\Delta^{2N}S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$, where $\Delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. As a consequence, we show that a conjecture of Etingof implies the conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra on the simplicity of the quotients $U({\mathfrak{vir}})/(C-c)$ of the enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra.

papers.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
papers.abstract: Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $\pi_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$. Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets. ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion. ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$. Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.

papers.title: Hilbert polynomials of configuration spaces over graphs of circumference at most 1
papers.abstract: The $ k $-configuration space $ B_k\Gamma $ of a topological space $ \Gamma $ is the space of sets of $ k $ distinct points in $ \Gamma $. In this paper, we consider the case where $ \Gamma $ is a graph of circumference at most $1$. We show that for all $ k\ge0 $, the $ i $-th Betti number of $ B_k\Gamma $ is given by a polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in $ k $, called the Hilbert polynomial of $ \Gamma $. We find an expression for the Hilbert polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in terms of those coming from the canonical $1$-bridge decomposition of $ \Gamma $. We also give a combinatorial description of the coefficients of $P_\Gamma^i(k)$.

papers.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
papers.abstract: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.

papers.title: Updating zigzag representatives efficiently
papers.abstract: Computation of zigzag persistence has progressed in recent years, with results showing that complexities of many problems closely align with those in the non-zigzag setting. The major efficiency gap now lies in the updating of zigzag representatives. In this paper, we propose efficient algorithms for updating zigzag representatives based on a recent algorithm for extracting zigzag representatives from a $R=DV$ decomposition of a constructed non-zigzag. The main difficulty for designing our update algorithms lies in the adjacency change occurring in two operations that lengthen or shorten a filtration. Despite the adjacency change, we find that the update can still be done efficiently in quadratic time.

papers.title: Notes on Milnor-Witt K-theory
papers.abstract: These notes develop the foundations of Milnor-Witt K-theory for fields of arbitrary characteristic, without any perfectness assumptions. Extending the work of Morel and Feld, we establish all functorial properties of Milnor-Witt K-theory with careful attention to twists. A main new contribution is the computation of transfers in the general, in particular inseparable, case using Grothendieck (differential) trace maps. The results provide a complete framework for the functoriality axioms of Milnor-Witt modules and form the basis for an upcoming work on Chow-Witt groups with Niels Feld and Fangzhou Jin.

papers.title: Cell decomposition and dual boundary complexes of character varieties
papers.abstract: The weak geometric P=W conjecture of Katzarkov--Noll--Pandit--Simpson asserts that for any smooth Betti moduli space $\mathcal{M}_B$ of complex dimension $d$ associated to a punctured Riemann surface, the dual boundary complex $\mathbb{D}\partial\mathcal{M}_B$ is homotopy equivalent to a $(d-1)$-sphere. Here, $\mathcal{M}_B$ is a generic $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$-character variety of genus $g$, with prescribed semisimple local monodromies at $k$ punctures. In this article, we prove the weak geometric P=W conjecture for all \emph{very generic} $\mathcal{M}_B$, namely when at least one conjugacy class is regular semisimple. A key step is a strengthening of Mellit's cell decomposition theorem: we decompose $\mathcal{M}_B$ itself (without passing to a vector bundle) into locally closed subvarieties which are stably isomorphic to $(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^{d-2b}\times \mathbb{C}^b$. A second ingredient is a motivic characterization of the integral cohomology of dual boundary complexes, developed in [Su24]. Following Simpson's strategy, the proof reduces to an inductive computation of dual boundary complexes arising from this cell decomposition.

papers.title: Higher order Massey products for algebras over algebraic operads
papers.abstract: We introduce higher-order Massey products for algebras over algebraic operads. This extends the work of Fernando Muro on secondary ones. We study their basic properties and behavior with respect to morphisms of algebras and operads and give some connections to formality. We prove that these higher-order operations represent the differentials in a naturally associated operadic Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence. We also study the interplay between particular choices of higher-order Massey products and quasi-isomorphic $\mathcal P_\infty$-structures on the homology of a $\mathcal P$-algebra. We focus on Koszul operads over a characteristic zero field and indicate how our results generalize to the non-Koszul case.

papers.title: Straightening for lax transformations and adjunctions of $(\infty,2)$-categories
papers.abstract: We prove an unstraightening result for lax transformations between functors from an arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-category to that of $(\infty,2)$-categories. We apply this to study partially (op)lax and weighted (co)limits, giving fibrational descriptions of such (co)limits for diagrams valued in $(\infty,2)$-categories, to characterize adjoints in $(\infty,2)$-categories of functors and (op)lax transformations, and to prove a mate correspondence between lax transformations that are componentwise right adjoints and oplax transformations that are componentwise left adjoints, for such transformations among functors between arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-categories.
